learn.title: Three classic bugs
learn.body: Memory bugs are undefined behavior: the program may crash, print wrong values, or even seem to work, and it can change from run to run or machine to machine. Because failures are random, learn to spot them by reading. Here are the three most common.

learn.title: Use after free
learn.body: The block was given back, then read. The pointer still holds an address, but the memory is not yours. The result is unpredictable. After freeing, set `p = NULL` so that a mistake fails loudly.

learn.title: Double free
learn.body: Freeing the same block twice corrupts the heap's bookkeeping. It often crashes, sometimes later and somewhere else. Setting `p = NULL` after the first free makes the second call harmless.

learn.title: Buffer overflow
learn.body: The block holds 3 ints, valid indexes 0, 1 and 2. Writing `a[3]` goes past its end and may overwrite other data. No error is reported at the write.

learn.title: Spot the bug
steps: Copying writes one byte past the block

learn.body: Code that appears to work is not proof of correctness. Tools such as Valgrind or the compiler option `-fsanitize=address` catch many of these bugs.
